body:
Re-ran with some retry logic, but it didn't work. Updated the bug report in the dropbox folder and pasted below

One note - maybe not the reason: I downloaded the appimage (1.26.7), then extracted the CLI from that using squashfs-root



# ART-cli aborts with uncaught `Exiv2::Error` ("Failed to read input data") when copying EXIF from a Leica M10-R DNG into its output


## Summary


`ART-cli` crashes (`SIGABRT`, uncaught C++ exception) very reliably while processing a
specific Leica M10-R DNG, with:


```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'Exiv2::Error'
  what():  Failed to read input data
```


**The strongest lead:** any invocation whose processing profile has `[MetaData] Mode=1`
(ART's "copy these EXIF tags from the original RAW into the output" setting) crashes this
file **11 times out of 12** attempts across a saved sidecar, a hand-trimmed sidecar, and an
unrelated bundled profile — all with `Mode=1`. Forcing `Mode=0` on an otherwise-identical
profile produced **4 clean exports out of 4** attempts. See Diagnostics below.


There is also a second, less-understood crash variant: with `-d` (default profile, no
sidecar at all) the crash instead happened immediately on opening the file, before any
`--progress` output — in 2 of 4 trials. It isn't yet confirmed whether this shares the
`Mode=1` codepath (ART's default profile may itself have metadata copy enabled) or is a
separate issue elsewhere in ART-cli's Exiv2 usage — flagging it rather than papering over
it, since the two crash sites produce identical error text but fire at very different
points in the run.


## Environment


- ART version: 1.26.7 (official Linux AppImage build)
- OS: Fedora Linux, kernel `7.1.3-201.fc44.x86_64`
- Source files are on an NFS mount, but confirmed **not** a factor (see Diagnostics)
- Bundled `libexiv2.so.28` inside the AppImage reports version **0.28.8**
- System-installed `exiv2` (separate, not used by ART) is version **0.28.6**, for comparison


## Files


Two DNGs from the same Leica M10-R, same session, similar size — one reliably triggers
the crash, the other does not:


- **Crashes**: `20260712_15-29-24.DNG` (~52 MB, 7872×5208)
- **Does not crash**: `20260712_14-35-23.DNG` (~47 MB, 7872×5208)


Both: Make=`Leica Camera AG`, Model=`LEICA M10-R`, Firmware/Software=`30.25.50.34`.


(Files available on request — not attached here.)


## Steps to reproduce


```sh
# With a saved .arp sidecar next to the DNG (produced by editing+saving in the ART GUI,
# [MetaData] Mode=1 in the saved profile) - crashed 4/4 attempts:
ART-cli -o out.jpg -j92 -Y -V --progress -s -c 20260712_15-29-24.DNG


# With no sidecar at all, using only the default profile - crashed 2/4 attempts, but at a
# different point (immediately on open, not during metadata copy - see Summary):
ART-cli -o out.jpg -j92 -Y -V --progress -d -c 20260712_15-29-24.DNG


# Applying an arbitrary bundled profile via -p (also Mode=1) - crashed 1/2 attempts:
ART-cli -o out.jpg -j92 -Y -V --progress -p "Portra 400.arp" -c 20260712_15-29-24.DNG


# The same saved sidecar, hand-edited so only "[MetaData] Mode=1" is changed to
# "Mode=0" (everything else byte-identical) - 0/4 crashes:
ART-cli -o out.jpg -j92 -Y -p sidecar-with-mode0.arp -c 20260712_15-29-24.DNG
```


Running the exact same command repeatedly against `20260712_15-29-24.DNG` gives a mix of
clean exits and crashes for every `Mode=1` variant tried (11 crashes across 12 attempts
total, pooling the `-s`, hand-trimmed-sidecar, and `-p "Portra 400.arp"` runs) - so not
strictly deterministic, but close to it in practice. The `Mode=0` variant has not crashed
in 4/4 attempts. `20260712_14-35-23.DNG` has not been observed to crash across a smaller
set of trials (2 attempts, both `-d`), so it's a plausible "doesn't reproduce as often on
this file" comparison point rather than a confirmed-clean file.


## Example crash output


```
ART, version 1.26.7, command line.
  Processing: .../20260712_15-29-24.DNG
  Merging default raw processing profile.
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'Exiv2::Error'
  what():  Failed to read input data
[1]    <pid> Aborted (core dumped)  ART-cli ...
```


A separate run of the same command crashed later in processing instead:


```
...
80


85
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'Exiv2::Error'
  what():  Failed to read input data
[1]    <pid> Aborted (core dumped)  ART-cli ...
```


## Diagnostics already ruled out


1. **Not the `.arp` sidecar's content.** Reproduces with the real saved sidecar, with a
   hand-trimmed minimal sidecar (single `[MetaData]` section, 2 EXIF keys instead of the
   full list), and with a completely unrelated bundled profile (`-p "Portra 400.arp"`).
   Also reproduces with no sidecar at all (`-d`, default profile only).


2. **Not file corruption.** The system's independently-installed `exiv2` binary
   (v0.28.6) reads this file's full metadata cleanly, 10/10 runs:
   `exiv2 -pa 20260712_15-29-24.DNG` → exit 0 every time.


3. **Not disk/network I/O.** The file is fully page-cache-resident (bulk read completes
   in single-digit milliseconds at the time of testing), and the crash still occurs
   intermittently against the cached file. NFS server ping latency to the storage host is
   sub-millisecond and stable throughout testing.


4. **Not a bug in the bundled Exiv2 build itself.** Loaded ART's own bundled
   `libexiv2.so.28` (0.28.8) into the system `exiv2` CLI via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and pointed
   it at the same file: 5/5 clean reads, no crash. So the *library*, driven single-threaded
   by a different caller, handles this file's metadata without issue — the crash only
   shows up when `ART-cli` itself processes the file.


5. **Strongly correlated with `[MetaData] Mode=1`.** Taking the real saved sidecar and
   changing nothing except `Mode=1` → `Mode=0` (same profile otherwise) turned a file that
   had just crashed 4/4 times in a row into 4/4 clean exports. `Mode=1` is ART's own
   "re-read the RAW's EXIF via Exiv2 and copy specific tags into the output" step, which
   (per the `--progress` output) runs late in the pipeline, around 85% — matching where the
   `-s`/`-p` crashes were observed to abort.


Given (4) plus (5), this looks like a bug specifically in `ART-cli`'s `[MetaData] Mode=1`
metadata-copy-to-output step's use of Exiv2 — not file corruption, not Exiv2 itself, and
not (based on the evidence gathered here) simple disk/network I/O. The residual
non-determinism (11/12 rather than 12/12 crashes on the `Mode=1` side) and the separate
early-crash variant seen under plain `-d` (immediately on open, 2/4 trials, not obviously
tied to `Mode=1` at all) suggest either a race condition in how/when that step touches the
`Exiv2::Image` object relative to other pipeline work, or more than one distinct bug
sharing the same generic Exiv2 exception text - both are plausible from what's been
isolated so far and worth keeping separate during investigation rather than assuming a
single root cause.


## Impact


Any headless/scripted use of `ART-cli` with metadata copy-back enabled (`[MetaData]
Mode=1`, which is ART's default when copying to a sidecar-driven export) against affected
files is unreliable to the point of being effectively broken — the same invocation
crashes (uncaught C++ exception, `SIGABRT`) on the large majority of runs, with no graceful
error path for a calling application to work around beyond disabling that feature entirely.


## Suggested next steps for maintainers


- Start with the `[MetaData] Mode=1` copy-to-output code path specifically (the step that
  re-reads the original RAW's EXIF via Exiv2 late in processing, ~85% through) - this is
  the most reliably reproducible trigger found so far (11/12 crashes with it enabled, 0/4
  with it disabled on an otherwise-identical profile).
- Separately check whether the default raw processing profile used by plain `-d` also has
  `Mode=1` set - if so, the early-open-time crash seen under `-d` may be the same bug
  firing at a different call site; if not, treat it as a second, distinct issue rather than
  assuming one fix covers both.
- Audit where that code path reads/writes the `Exiv2::Image` metadata relative to other
  threads that may hold or use the same image object concurrently (demosaic/output-encode
  workers, `-V`/`--progress` reporting, etc.) for a missing lock or a use-after-free/dangling
  reference - a debug build under ThreadSanitizer/Valgrind reproducing this file's crash
  would likely surface it quickly given how reliably it reproduces and how cleanly it's
  isolated from Exiv2 itself.
